config.title: Performance & profiling

intro.title: Performance & profiling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js application to measure and analyze the performance of a function. You will learn the core concept of profiling, which involves timing code execution to identify bottlenecks. The main technologies involved include Node.js's built-in `console.time` and `console.timeEnd` methods for basic performance measurement. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to make your code more efficient by tracking its speed.
intro.usecase: Performance profiling is essential for optimizing Node.js applications in production environments like e-commerce platforms, where slow API responses directly impact sales. Developers use profiling tools to identify bottlenecks in database queries, third-party API calls, or memory leaks in real-time dashboards that monitor user activity. For example, profiling helps optimize checkout flows by pinpointing slow payment gateway integrations or inefficient inventory lookup operations. This practice ensures applications remain responsive under heavy traffic, such as during flash sales or peak user sessions.

objectives: Initialize the Node.js built-in performance measurement APIs
Construct performance timers to measure execution time of code blocks
Apply memory usage monitoring to identify potential leaks
Configure the Node.js profiler to generate performance reports
Manipulate profiling data to analyze CPU bottlenecks
Integrate performance hooks to track asynchronous operations
Implement basic performance optimization techniques based on profiling results

steps.instruction: Import the performance hooks module and console module for timing measurements. Use the built-in Node.js 'perf_hooks' and 'console' modules.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import both modules. The 'perf_hooks' module contains performance measurement APIs.

successCriteria: Both 'perf_hooks' and 'console' modules are imported using require() statements.

steps.title: Add event loop monitoring
steps.instruction: Inside the main function, add code to measure event loop latency using performance hooks. Create a function called measureEventLoopLatency that uses performance.mark and performance.measure to track the delay between setTimeout calls.
steps.hint: You can create a function that uses performance.mark('start'), then setTimeout to call performance.mark('end') and performance.measure('eventLoopLatency', 'start', 'end').

successCriteria: A measureEventLoopLatency function is defined inside main() that uses performance.mark and performance.measure to track event loop latency.
